title: The Cost of Social Norms
coreMove: Identify the norm in force before introducing money, because a tiny payment can reclassify the whole relationship.
sourcePressure: The source contrasts social norms and market norms, showing how small payments can crowd out goodwill and make a relationship transactional.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: The weak version says incentives backfire; the precise lesson is that money can move the interaction from social reciprocity to market pricing.

exampleSpecs.domain: blood-donation mobile clinic changing thank-you gifts into cash cards
exampleSpecs.audience: a clinic coordinator deciding how to recognize repeat donors
exampleSpecs.stakes: reducing donor identity by making the visit feel like a low-paid errand
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the coordinator compares the sign-up sheet after the thank-you pin is replaced by a small cash card and sees regular donors hesitate at the table
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a folding table with donor pins in one tray and cash cards in another

exampleSpecs.domain: neighborhood snow-shoveling rota after a storm
exampleSpecs.audience: a block captain deciding whether to fine households that skip their turn
exampleSpecs.stakes: turning mutual aid into a cheap service residents can buy out of
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the captain reads the proposed fine aloud, then asks whether residents will hear it as a penalty or as the price of staying inside
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a clipboard of shoveled addresses resting on a snowbank at dusk

exampleSpecs.audience: a maintainer deciding whether to add tiny bounties to every volunteer task
exampleSpecs.stakes: making expert contributors price work they used to treat as stewardship
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the maintainer watches a volunteer ignore the bounty amount and ask whether the project still trusts unpaid review
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a terminal window beside a bounty spreadsheet on a late-night video call

exampleSpecs.domain: choir section leaders asked to coach new singers
exampleSpecs.audience: a music director deciding between handwritten thanks and per-session payments
exampleSpecs.stakes: turning a shared musical duty into a low hourly wage comparison
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the director places thank-you notes and payment envelopes on the piano, then notices which one makes the section leaders start calculating hours
exampleSpecs.firstImage: sealed envelopes lined along the edge of an upright piano

exampleSpecs.domain: mutual-aid freezer meal network after surgery
exampleSpecs.audience: a neighbor organizing meals for a recovering resident
exampleSpecs.stakes: making care feel like catering when someone suggests reimbursing every casserole
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: the organizer writes a grocery reimbursement line, then crosses it out and replaces it with dietary notes and a thank-you call
exampleSpecs.firstImage: foil-covered freezer meals stacked in a cooler by an apartment lobby

exampleSpecs.audience: a club board deciding whether to charge members for setting up telescopes at public nights
exampleSpecs.stakes: weakening the pride of sharing the sky by pricing the setup duty too cheaply
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: after a per-telescope payment is announced, the board hears members ask whether the amount includes teardown, revealing the norm has shifted
exampleSpecs.firstImage: tripod legs folded on a dark field beside a red flashlight

skillTargets: distinguish social norm cues from market norm cues
predict when a small payment will crowd out goodwill
redesign recognition without pricing the favor
explain why returning to social norms can be difficult

tryThisNowSpec: Before offering money for a favor, name whether the moment is running on reciprocity or exchange; if it is reciprocity, choose a nonprice sign of appreciation instead.
